# Statedoku, full reference

> Statedoku is a free daily US geography puzzle: a 3×3 grid where every cell must hold a US state that satisfies both its row clue and its column clue. The site also has 21 free geography games (map clicking, capitals, abbreviations, flags, history) and reference pages on the 50 states, in English, French and Spanish. Free, no signup.

Last updated: 2026-10-15. Generated from the site's own data (data/states.json) and pages. Site: https://statedoku.com

## 1. What Statedoku is

A free daily browser puzzle that teaches US geography, online since May 2026, with daily puzzles since 1 June 2026. Besides the daily grid the site has 21 free geography games and reference pages on the 50 states, in English, French and Spanish.

Statedoku is made by Moses Tounby. That is a pen name for a solo developer based in France. It is an independent project with no company, team or investor behind it, and it is not affiliated with the New York Times, Wordle or any publisher.

## 2. Rules of the daily puzzle

1. One 3×3 grid a day. Three clues run across the top and three down the side, such as "Borders Mexico", "Admitted in 1900s" or "Name ends in A".
2. Every cell needs a US state that satisfies both its row clue and its column clue. No state may be used twice in the same grid.
3. Any state that fits both clues is accepted, not only one intended answer. Each grid is checked to have exactly one complete solution, so it can be solved by reasoning rather than guessing.
4. Because any fitting state is accepted, a state placed early can be the one another cell needed. Filled cells therefore stay editable, and the picker has a "Clear this cell" button. Clearing costs nothing.
5. Five mistakes a day. A mistake is a state that fails one of its two clues, or one already used elsewhere in the grid. After the fifth, the puzzle ends and shows every state that would have worked in each cell.
6. A new grid appears at midnight in the player's local time. Everyone playing the same date gets the same grid. Past grids, from 1 June 2026, stay playable in the archive.
7. To pick a state, type at least four letters of its name. Abbreviations are not searched.
8. Free, in the browser, no signup and no download. English, French and Spanish.

Full rules: https://statedoku.com/how-to-play/

## 3. The 21 games

Free, no signup, playable on a phone. English address, then French and Spanish.

- **Place the State**: Click the named state on a blank US map. Easy (5 well-known states), Normal (10) or Hard (15, lookalikes included), 3 lives. https://statedoku.com/play/place-the-state/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/place-the-state/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/place-the-state/)
- **USPS Abbreviations Quiz**: Match the 2-letter postal code to its US state. 20 rounds, multiple choice. https://statedoku.com/play/state-abbreviations/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/state-abbreviations/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/state-abbreviations/)
- **State Capitals Match**: Match 10 US states with their capitals. https://statedoku.com/play/state-capitals-match/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/state-capitals-match/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/state-capitals-match/)
- **State Silhouettes**: Guess the US state from its outline alone. https://statedoku.com/play/state-silhouettes/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/state-silhouettes/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/state-silhouettes/)
- **States Connections**: NYT-Connections style: group 16 US states into 4 hidden categories. https://statedoku.com/play/states-connections/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/states-connections/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/states-connections/)
- **State Capitals Quiz**: Type the capital of each US state. https://statedoku.com/play/state-capitals-typing/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/state-capitals-typing/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/state-capitals-typing/)
- **Biggest City Quiz**: Identify the biggest city of each US state. https://statedoku.com/play/biggest-cities/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/biggest-cities/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/biggest-cities/)
- **State Flags Quiz**: Identify a state from its flag description. https://statedoku.com/play/state-flags/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/state-flags/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/state-flags/)
- **13 Original Colonies**: Click all 13 original American colonies on the US map. https://statedoku.com/play/thirteen-colonies/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/thirteen-colonies/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/thirteen-colonies/)
- **State Admission Order**: Order 8 states by their year of admission to the Union. https://statedoku.com/play/state-admission-order/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/state-admission-order/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/state-admission-order/)
- **Confederate States Quiz**: Click all 11 Confederate states of the US Civil War on the map. https://statedoku.com/play/confederate-states/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/confederate-states/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/confederate-states/)
- **Presidents by State**: Match US presidents to their state of birth. https://statedoku.com/play/president-birth-states/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/president-birth-states/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/president-birth-states/)
- **State Nicknames Quiz**: Match nicknames to their states: Lone Star, Golden State, Sunshine State. https://statedoku.com/play/state-nicknames/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/state-nicknames/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/state-nicknames/)
- **State Mottos Quiz**: Match each state to its official motto. https://statedoku.com/play/state-mottos/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/state-mottos/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/state-mottos/)
- **State Symbols Quiz**: Match state birds, flowers, and trees to their US state. https://statedoku.com/play/state-symbols/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/state-symbols/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/state-symbols/)
- **Time Zones Quiz**: Identify the time zone of each US state. https://statedoku.com/play/time-zones/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/time-zones/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/time-zones/)
- **Border States Quiz**: Click all states bordering Canada or Mexico on the US map. https://statedoku.com/play/border-states/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/border-states/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/border-states/)
- **Rivers & Mountains**: Match US rivers and mountain landmarks to their states. https://statedoku.com/play/rivers-mountains/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/rivers-mountains/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/rivers-mountains/)
- **Electoral College Quiz**: Test how many electoral votes each state has. https://statedoku.com/play/electoral-college/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/electoral-college/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/electoral-college/)
- **Swing States Quiz**: Click all 7 swing states of 2024 on the US map. https://statedoku.com/play/swing-states/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/swing-states/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/swing-states/)
- **No Income Tax Quiz**: Click all 9 US states with no state income tax. https://statedoku.com/play/no-income-tax-states/ (FR https://statedoku.com/fr/play/no-income-tax-states/, ES https://statedoku.com/es/play/no-income-tax-states/)

## 4. The 50 states

USPS code, capital, largest city, Census region, year admitted to the Union (for the original 13, the year it ratified the Constitution).

- **Alabama** (AL): capital Montgomery; largest city Huntsville; South; admitted 1819.
- **Alaska** (AK): capital Juneau; largest city Anchorage; West; admitted 1959.
- **Arizona** (AZ): capital Phoenix; largest city Phoenix; West; admitted 1912.
- **Arkansas** (AR): capital Little Rock; largest city Little Rock; South; admitted 1836.
- **California** (CA): capital Sacramento; largest city Los Angeles; West; admitted 1850.
- **Colorado** (CO): capital Denver; largest city Denver; West; admitted 1876.
- **Connecticut** (CT): capital Hartford; largest city Bridgeport; Northeast; admitted 1788.
- **Delaware** (DE): capital Dover; largest city Wilmington; South; admitted 1787.
- **Florida** (FL): capital Tallahassee; largest city Jacksonville; South; admitted 1845.
- **Georgia** (GA): capital Atlanta; largest city Atlanta; South; admitted 1788.
- **Hawaii** (HI): capital Honolulu; largest city Honolulu; West; admitted 1959.
- **Idaho** (ID): capital Boise; largest city Boise; West; admitted 1890.
- **Illinois** (IL): capital Springfield; largest city Chicago; Midwest; admitted 1818.
- **Indiana** (IN): capital Indianapolis; largest city Indianapolis; Midwest; admitted 1816.
- **Iowa** (IA): capital Des Moines; largest city Des Moines; Midwest; admitted 1846.
- **Kansas** (KS): capital Topeka; largest city Wichita; Midwest; admitted 1861.
- **Kentucky** (KY): capital Frankfort; largest city Louisville; South; admitted 1792.
- **Louisiana** (LA): capital Baton Rouge; largest city New Orleans; South; admitted 1812.
- **Maine** (ME): capital Augusta; largest city Portland; Northeast; admitted 1820.
- **Maryland** (MD): capital Annapolis; largest city Baltimore; South; admitted 1788.
- **Massachusetts** (MA): capital Boston; largest city Boston; Northeast; admitted 1788.
- **Michigan** (MI): capital Lansing; largest city Detroit; Midwest; admitted 1837.
- **Minnesota** (MN): capital Saint Paul; largest city Minneapolis; Midwest; admitted 1858.
- **Mississippi** (MS): capital Jackson; largest city Jackson; South; admitted 1817.
- **Missouri** (MO): capital Jefferson City; largest city Kansas City; Midwest; admitted 1821.
- **Montana** (MT): capital Helena; largest city Billings; West; admitted 1889.
- **Nebraska** (NE): capital Lincoln; largest city Omaha; Midwest; admitted 1867.
- **Nevada** (NV): capital Carson City; largest city Las Vegas; West; admitted 1864.
- **New Hampshire** (NH): capital Concord; largest city Manchester; Northeast; admitted 1788.
- **New Jersey** (NJ): capital Trenton; largest city Newark; Northeast; admitted 1787.
- **New Mexico** (NM): capital Santa Fe; largest city Albuquerque; West; admitted 1912.
- **New York** (NY): capital Albany; largest city New York City; Northeast; admitted 1788.
- **North Carolina** (NC): capital Raleigh; largest city Charlotte; South; admitted 1789.
- **North Dakota** (ND): capital Bismarck; largest city Fargo; Midwest; admitted 1889.
- **Ohio** (OH): capital Columbus; largest city Columbus; Midwest; admitted 1803.
- **Oklahoma** (OK): capital Oklahoma City; largest city Oklahoma City; South; admitted 1907.
- **Oregon** (OR): capital Salem; largest city Portland; West; admitted 1859.
- **Pennsylvania** (PA): capital Harrisburg; largest city Philadelphia; Northeast; admitted 1787.
- **Rhode Island** (RI): capital Providence; largest city Providence; Northeast; admitted 1790.
- **South Carolina** (SC): capital Columbia; largest city Charleston; South; admitted 1788.
- **South Dakota** (SD): capital Pierre; largest city Sioux Falls; Midwest; admitted 1889.
- **Tennessee** (TN): capital Nashville; largest city Nashville; South; admitted 1796.
- **Texas** (TX): capital Austin; largest city Houston; South; admitted 1845.
- **Utah** (UT): capital Salt Lake City; largest city Salt Lake City; West; admitted 1896.
- **Vermont** (VT): capital Montpelier; largest city Burlington; Northeast; admitted 1791.
- **Virginia** (VA): capital Richmond; largest city Virginia Beach; South; admitted 1788.
- **Washington** (WA): capital Olympia; largest city Seattle; West; admitted 1889.
- **West Virginia** (WV): capital Charleston; largest city Charleston; South; admitted 1863.
- **Wisconsin** (WI): capital Madison; largest city Milwaukee; Midwest; admitted 1848.
- **Wyoming** (WY): capital Cheyenne; largest city Cheyenne; West; admitted 1890.

## 5. Census regions

- **Northeast** (9): Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Vermont.
- **South** (16): Alabama, Arkansas, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia.
- **Midwest** (12): Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota, Wisconsin.
- **West** (13): Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington, Wyoming.

The South includes Delaware and Maryland. Washington, D.C. is counted in the South region but is not a state.

## 6. Key lists

**States bordering Canada (13)**: Alaska, Idaho, Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Montana, New Hampshire, New York, North Dakota, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Vermont, Washington. Ohio and Pennsylvania meet Canada across Lake Erie.

**States bordering Mexico (4)**: Arizona, California, New Mexico, Texas.

**The original 13 colonies (13)**: Connecticut, Delaware, Georgia, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Virginia.

**Confederate states (11)**: Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia.

**States with no broad personal income tax (9)**: Alaska, Florida, Nevada, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington, Wyoming. Washington taxes some capital gains; New Hampshire taxed interest and dividends until 2025.

**Landlocked states, with no ocean coast and no Great Lakes shore (20)**: Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Vermont, West Virginia, Wyoming.

**Capitals that are also the largest city of their state (17)**: Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Indiana, Iowa, Massachusetts, Mississippi, Ohio, Oklahoma, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Utah, West Virginia, Wyoming. In the other 33 states the capital is not the largest city.

## 7. Cities that are not states

Searches like "is Las Vegas a state" have one answer: it is a city, in a state.

- Las Vegas is the largest city of Nevada (capital: Carson City).
- Boston is the capital and the largest city of Massachusetts.
- Atlanta is the capital and the largest city of Georgia.
- Minneapolis is the largest city of Minnesota (capital: Saint Paul).
- Philadelphia is the largest city of Pennsylvania (capital: Harrisburg).
- Charlotte is the largest city of North Carolina (capital: Raleigh).
- Seattle is the largest city of Washington (capital: Olympia).
- Portland is the largest city of Maine (capital: Augusta), and also the largest city of Oregon (capital: Salem).
- Phoenix is the capital and the largest city of Arizona.
- Chicago is the largest city of Illinois (capital: Springfield).
- Houston is the largest city of Texas (capital: Austin).
- Los Angeles is the largest city of California (capital: Sacramento).
- New York City is the largest city of New York (capital: Albany).
- Detroit is the largest city of Michigan (capital: Lansing).
- Milwaukee is the largest city of Wisconsin (capital: Madison).
- Baltimore is the largest city of Maryland (capital: Annapolis).
- Washington State and Washington, D.C. are different places. The state's capital is Olympia.

## 8. Questions about the site

**Is Statedoku free?** Yes, with no signup and no account.

**Is there an app?** The site can be added to a phone's home screen. There is no app store version.

**Can it be used in class?** Yes. The daily puzzle and every game page have a "Share to Google Classroom" button, the games can be embedded with an iframe (https://statedoku.com/widgets/), and a printable map is at https://statedoku.com/learn/printable-us-states-map/.

**Is there an API?** A free JSON API with the 50 states is documented at https://statedoku.com/api/.

**Who makes it?** Statedoku is made by Moses Tounby. That is a pen name for a solo developer based in France. It is an independent project with no company, team or investor behind it, and it is not affiliated with the New York Times, Wordle or any publisher. Contact: contact@statedoku.com

**How to cite it?** Statedoku, daily US states puzzle. https://statedoku.com
